name: Bousso, 'Flat space physics from holography' (hep-th/0402058v2, 14 Aug 2004; JHEP 0405:050): the Bekenstein bound S <= 2 pi M R / hbar contains no Newton constant and remains nontrivial at G = 0

source.located: arXiv hep-th/0402058v2 (UCB-PTH-04/02, dated 14 Aug 2004), all 12 pages returned (abstract p.1; Sec 2.1 p.4; Sec 2.2 pp.5-6; Sec 3 pp.7-8; Sec 4 pp.9-10; refs pp.10-11). Journal ref JHEP 0405, 050 (2004) as cited by Casini 0804.2182 ref [7].
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(hep-th/0402058) returning full page text pp.1-12 on 2026-09-26; both phrases the tree quotes located verbatim (abstract p.1 and Sec 2.2 p.5)

published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'In flat space, the covariant entropy bound reduces to the Bekenstein bound. The latter does not contain Newton's constant and cannot operate via gravitational backreaction.' Sec 2.2 (p.5): 'In its original form, the bound states that the entropy S of any weakly gravitating matter system obeys S <= 2 pi M R/hbar, (2.2) where M is the total gravitating mass of the matter and R is the radius of the smallest sphere that barely fits around the system. The absence of Newton's constant in Bekenstein's bound is notable. It renders Eq. (2.2) independent of the strength of gravity, G, in its regime of validity. In particular, the bound remains nontrivial when gravity is turned off completely (G = 0). Therefore, gravitational physics cannot play a role in upholding it, quite unlike the case of the holographic bound.' Weak-gravity condition (2.3): M << R/G. Sec 2.1 (p.4): the covariant bound A/4G hbar 'becom[es] more lenient as G -> 0, and trivial for G = 0'. Sec 3 (p.3, p.8): the GCEB gives S <~ M R/(l_Pl^2/G) (3.2), 'the Bekenstein bound (up to factors of order one)', which 'involves only the combination l_Pl^2/G'. p.8: 'our understanding of the Bekenstein bound is still imperfect. The bound is quite sensitive to the precise definition of the entropy'; species problem for the formulations of refs [19,20]. p.10: 'To go further and obtain an exact equality, hbar = l_Pl^2/G, one would need at least one example of a system that precisely saturates the Bekenstein bound with this value. This is an important outstanding problem.'
published_hypotheses: H1 WEAKLY GRAVITATING matter system: M << R/G (eq 2.3); the G-independence is asserted 'in its regime of validity' (p.5), and the whole derivation 'applies only in weakly gravitating regions' (p.3)
H2 M = total gravitating mass; R = radius of the smallest sphere that barely fits around the system (p.5)

H3 hbar is the constant held fixed: the statement is written in the hbar-form (2.2); Sec 2 is a review that 'permit[s] ourselves to write the Bekenstein bound in terms of hbar' (p.3). In the source's own axiomatic form (3.2), with l_Pl primitive, the bound reads S <~ M R G/l_Pl^2

H5 entropy S = log of the number of independent Fock-space states compatible with the geometric boundary conditions (p.2); the source flags that the bound is 'quite sensitive to the precise definition of the entropy' and that a rigorous formulation is assumed to exist (p.8)

H6 (for the derivation, not for the quoted claim) the generalized covariant entropy bound (GCEB, eq 2.4) as axiom; the Sec-3 derivation is a simplified order-unity argument, the rigorous one being ref [17] hep-th/0210295

This bears on the K = 0 justification (a different key: Bekenstein 1981 / black-hole saturation), NOT on the G coordinate.

rederivation.outcome: 12/12 checks agree with the source. (a) dS_Bek/dG = 0 in the hbar-form; (a') nonzero at G = 0; (b) A/4G hbar -> infinity as G -> 0 ('trivial', p.4); (c) S_Bek/S_hol = 2GM/R exactly, so Bekenstein is tighter iff M << R/G (eq 2.3); (d) Schwarzschild R = 2GM saturates 2 pi M R/hbar EXACTLY, but (d') has M/(R/G) = 1/2, outside the stated regime; (e) 2GM -> 0 as G -> 0; (f,f') in the source's own l_Pl-form S = 2 pi G M R/l_Pl^2, G appears and the G -> 0 limit is 0 -- the 'no G' reading holds under hbar held fixed; (g) the Sec-3 X-ray heuristic with deflection 4GM/R and lever arm R reproduces 2 pi M R/hbar (lever arm is an order-unity choice made here; the source claims only 'up to factors of order one'). Numeric (h): electron holographic figure computed 1.8e45-7.1e46 vs printed 10^44 -- a discrepancy, not an error. Separately, bounds.py's own selftest (run read-only) passes the pins that rest on this key: 'ONE bound has gravity in it, and it is Bousso' and 'TWO entropy bounds carry no Newton constant'.

later_literature.ref: Casini, 'Relative entropy and the Bekenstein bound', arXiv:0804.2182 (CQG 25 (2008) 205021)
later_literature.what: Gives a well-defined flat-space QFT statement, S_V - S_V^0 <= K_V - K_V^0, i.e. positivity of relative entropy (eqs 17-18), proven, free of the species problem, with no G anywhere; approaches (1) with lambda = 2 pi for an object far from the Rindler boundary. This makes 'nontrivial with gravity off' a theorem for that formulation. It also CONFIRMS H1's restriction: relative entropy 'can only be defined in a fixed geometry, and becomes ill defined once the backreaction is included ... the static limit is crucial, what means a flat space limit for the Bekenstein bound' (p.8). And: 'no general consensus on the correct value of lambda or the meaning of R' (p.3). Cites Bousso hep-th/0402058 as ref [7] for 'what is behind protecting the bound are primarily the uncertainty relations'.

later_literature.ref: Hayden & Wang, 'What exactly does Bekenstein bound?', arXiv:2309.07436v3 (2025)
later_literature.what: States the bound as S <= lambda R E with 'lambda some order-one constant independent of G_N' (eq 1.1) and calls Casini's form 'a widely accepted proven version'. It NARROWS a different reading (the bound as a universal limit on information: zero-bit capacity of the Unruh channel is unbounded in species number when only the decoder is restricted), which the tree does not use; the G-independence is untouched.
The rigorous GCEB -> Bekenstein derivation for weakly gravitating systems that hep-th/0402058 Sec 3 simplifies (restated at p.6-8 of hep-th/0402058).
The original bound; restated by Bousso p.5 and Casini p.1 (derived from the GSL via a black-hole gedankenexperiment -- the provenance DOCKET.md:184-186 cites for the old G = 1).

lacked_data: The result is a structural statement about which constants appear in eq (2.2); it rests on no measured datum, so there was no datum to lack. What came later is theory, not data: Casini (2008) supplied the rigorous flat-space QFT formulation Bousso's p.8 said was missing, and it CONFIRMS the conclusion -- the relative-entropy bound contains no G and is proven with gravity absent. The later work equally confirms the hypothesis the tree drops: Casini p.8 says the formulation needs a fixed (static, flat-limit) geometry and fails once backreaction is included. The one numerical example (electron holographic bound) is off by 1.3-2.9 decades against a recomputation with CODATA 2022 constants, but those constants have not moved materially since 2004 (G identical 2018/2022; hbar exact since 2019), so the discrepancy is not a lacked-data effect, and it does not touch the claim. Evidence on M's hypothesis for this result: none in its favour, and the later rigorous work runs against it (strengthens the result).
grade_evidence: The two phrases bounds.py:310-312 quotes are verbatim in the source (abstract p.1; Sec 2.2 p.5), and every closed-form claim re-derives (12/12 sympy checks). The claim the tree uses -- no G in S <= 2 pi R E, hence G = 0 under the syntactic rule bounds.py:27 -- STANDS in the form the source states it, and the pins resting on it (bounds.py:459, 469, 528, 538-539) pass and do not move. The grade is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the source asserts G-independence 'in its regime of validity' for 'any weakly gravitating matter system' (M << R/G, eq 2.3) and writes it with hbar held fixed, and the tree drops both qualifiers (bounds.py:309-312; DOCKET.md:193-195). The dropped regime matters inside the same row: the tree pairs the G-free quote with black-hole saturation (bounds.py:312-313, 315; DOCKET.md:196-201), but a black hole has M/(R/G) = 1/2 (computed), lies outside that regime, and does not exist at G = 0; within the regime, the source calls a precise saturating example 'an important outstanding problem' (p.10). That weakens the K = 0 'known saturated' justification the DOCKET 4 note leans on, which belongs to a different key and is not graded here. Not WRONG: no counterexample or contradiction to the source was found. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the hypotheses under which it uses the key -- 'weakly gravitating system, M << R/G; hbar-form' -- beside the quote at bounds.py:309-312 and in the canonical entry, and either drops 'saturated by black holes' as a support for K = 0 or names it as a strong-gravity fact outside Bousso's regime (e.g. citing Casini's asymptotic flat-space saturation, 0804.2182 eqs 43-44, instead). To WRONG: a reading of the source or a computation showing (2.2) contains G in its hbar-form, or that it becomes trivial at G = 0 with hbar fixed -- the rederive checks show the opposite. The electron 10^44 discrepancy cannot move the grade; the tree does not use it.
